personality: 7 Dark-First Utility with 6 Glass / Luxe cinematic surfaces
personality_one_liner: A persistent, cinematic medieval command center where dark slate, glass HUDs, and antique gold accents make deep resource management and tactical deployment feel premium and deeply immersive.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing around map overlays to prevent accidental touches; tight data-heavy spacing in dashboards for resource counters.

do's: Use heavy tinted glass for HUD overlays on top of the 3D map (safe-area aware)
Bottom sheets for target selection and quick actions
Sticky resource top bar overlaying the map
dont's: Inner cards in the settlement dashboard

screens.name: Login & World Selection
screens.purpose: Authenticate player and let them pick their persistent server (World).
screens.layout: Full-bleed dark medieval castle background with vertical linear gradient scrim (0% top -> 80% surface bottom). Login fields in a glass container at the lower third. World selection uses large cards with server status (warning color for high pop, success for stable).

screens.name: 3D World Map (Default Tab)
screens.purpose: Primary gameplay view. Expo-GL full-screen canvas showing isometric chunks, overlaid with a touch-friendly HUD.

states.error: Retry connection button over cached terrain

screens.layout: Z-index 0: The 3D canvas (Three.js). Z-index 1: Top safe-area sticky resource bar (glass). Bottom right: compact floating action button for quick-locate. Bottom safe-area: Tab bar (glass). Tapping a neutral or enemy territory triggers a @gorhom/bottom-sheet with target details and 'March' primary CTA.

screens.name: Settlement Dashboard
screens.purpose: Manage buildings, resources, and construction queues.
screens.layout: Top section: 2-column live resource grid. Middle section: 2 construction queues with progress bars. Bottom section: Wrap grid of building tiles with level badges and upgrade status indicators.

screens.name: Building Detail Card (Bottom Sheet/Modal)
screens.purpose: Drill-down to see upgrade costs, requirements, and state.
screens.layout: Heavy hierarchy. Large building title (EB Garamond) + current/next level. List of requirements (resources, preceding buildings) using success/error token colors based on availability. Sticky CTA at the bottom for 'Upgrade'.

screens.name: Army & Recruitment
screens.purpose: Train 13 types of units and manage producer queues.

states.empty: Illustration of empty barracks + 'No troops recruited' text.

screens.layout: Tabbed view (Troops / Recruitment). Recruitment shows horizontal scroll of unit cards (batch slider input) + active training queues. Use tabular numbers (Manrope) for unit stats and timers.

screens.name: Research Tree
screens.purpose: Navigate 12 branches and 114 nodes for empire upgrades.
screens.layout: Pan-and-zoom 2D grid/tree using gesture handler. Nodes indicate states via border colors (brandPrimary for available, muted for locked, success for researched). Sticky footer showing 2 active research queues.

screens.name: March Composition
screens.purpose: Select units for missions (Attack, Raid, Conquest) and see ETA.

states.empty: No idle troops available to march.

screens.layout: Mission type segmented control at top. List of available unit sliders to assign troops. Bottom fixed container showing ETA (info token), march speed, and 'Send March' CTA (brandPrimary).

screens.name: Battle Reports & Inbox
screens.purpose: Review combat outcomes, scout reports, and system events.
screens.layout: Chronological list of cards. Battle reports use victory (success) or defeat (error) color edge-bars on the left of the card. Detail view shows side-by-side casualty comparisons.

login_bg.alt: Epic dark medieval stone structure with volumetric lighting

instructions_to_main_agent: Load EB Garamond (heading) and Manrope (UI/metrics) locally using expo-font. Do not use @expo-google-fonts.

Implement the 3D map using expo-gl + three.js. The HUD must sit on top of the GLView canvas in a completely separate absolute-positioned layer to ensure touch events work (hitSlop) without blocking map interaction.
Bilingual support (IT/EN) is mandatory. Abstract all textual content into a translation dictionary (e.g., i18n-js or a custom context) from the start.

Timers are everywhere (building queues, research queues, marching ETA). Create a highly reusable, performant countdown component that avoids React re-renders on every tick (e.g., reanimated or local state).
HUD overlays must heavily rely on expo-blur with the specified 'glass' platform overrides to maintain contrast over the chaotic 3D terrain.
Strictly follow the color token palette: absolutely NO BLUES, no purples. Use the custom tokens provided for resources (grain/wood/clay/iron/gold) and terrain.
On bottom sheets, ensure safe area insets are respected so the main CTA doesn't conflict with Android's home indicator.
